comment: Every real checkpoint the parity and triage suites load, with the source that serves it and the converter that puts it in the module's layout. `fetch.py` reads this. Sizes are the bytes the source reported when the entry was added; a mismatch means the source changed under us, which is worth knowing before a parity number moves. Most assets download from `url`; `gdrive` names a Google Drive file id and `extract` a member path inside a zip at `url`, for the two releases served no other way.

assets.note: the x3 release: ONE ×3 pixel-shuffle stage where x4 runs two ×2 stages, so it fits only the x3 geometry

Silero VAD v6 (snakers4). The released .jit carries a 16 kHz `_model.*` branch and an 8 kHz `_model_8k.*` branch; the converter keeps the 16 kHz branch. The parity record is produced by `run_reference.py silero_vad` under the llm oracle env, which needs the `silero-vad` package (its wrapper streams 512-sample chunks and threads the LSTM state); the converter needs only torch. `bytes` pins the master file, so a drift fails loudly.

The Descript Audio Codec, 44.1 kHz 8 kbps (9 codebooks). The released `.pth` wraps a weight-normalized `state_dict`; the converter extracts it in PyTorch layout and the loader fuses and transposes. The parity record is produced by `run_reference.py dac` under the llm oracle env, which needs the `descript-audio-codec` package (the encode/decode reference); the converter needs only torch.

SNAC 24 kHz multi-scale speech codec (3 codebooks at strides [4,2,1], depthwise convs, a decoder noise block, no bottleneck attention). The release's convolutions are weight-normalized through torch's parametrization API (`parametrizations.weight.original0/1`); the converter keeps them and the loader fuses. The parity record is produced by `run_reference.py snac` under the llm oracle env (needs `snac`), with the decoder noise block disabled so the reconstruction is deterministic.

SigLIP 2 base-patch16-224, the CLIP upgrade / VLM vision tower. The release is ALREADY a PyTorch-layout safetensors the loader reads directly (transposing the 4-D patch conv, mapping the vision_model./text_model. prefixes), so the converter is a passthrough normalizer. Most of the 1.5 GB is the 256k multilingual text embedding table. Parity via `run_reference.py siglip2` (llm oracle env, transformers >= 4.51). The architecture is SigLIP v1 (model_type 'siglip'); '2' is the training.

Tiny AutoEncoder for SD, the fast preview decoder. TWO release files (taesd_encoder.pth + taesd_decoder.pth, GitHub, ~5 MB each); the converter combines them into encoder.*/decoder.* keys and the [Module]-array loader matches the numeric Sequential keys directly. Parity via `run_reference.py taesd` (madebyollin's own taesd.py, vendored in sources/).

The LTX-Video causal 3D VAE, the first stage of the video-generation path. The release is already a PyTorch-layout safetensors the loader reads directly (transposing 5-D Conv3d weights, causal-conv wrapper keeps the .conv key). Parity via `run_reference.py ltx_vae` under the ltx oracle env (diffusers >= 0.32); it loads the VAE from IK_LTX_VAE_DIR.

A photograph with a human face, for NFKMLXFaceAlignment's detection and paste-back tests. NASA Apollo XI portrait (photo ID S69-31741), a work of the US government and therefore public domain — Wikimedia records it as not copyrighted. The general validation plate (IK_VAL_IMAGE) is an animal, so it cannot serve here.
The face detector the CodeFormer reference pipeline runs through facexlib. mobile0.25 is 1.7 MB, so the parity-exact alignment path costs almost nothing beside CodeFormer's own checkpoint.
The .pt wraps the state dict under a `model` key; names pass through.
The .pt wraps the state dict under a `model` key; names pass through.
The .pt wraps the state dict under a `model` key; names pass through.

The official jik876 UNIVERSAL_V1 generator (the repo mirrors the Google Drive release). Weight-normalized; the converter fuses g*v/||v||, which is remove_weight_norm. The config beside it must be saved as hifigan_universal_v1_config.json for the oracle.

The vocoder PAIRED with the espnet FastSpeech2 release - trained on its normalized mels, where the universal jik876 generator expects raw log-mels and produces loud garbage (Whisper hears '(indistinct)'). The converter strips the vocoder. prefix; weight norm is already fused.
The LJSpeech conformer FastSpeech2. Names pass through; the converter drops the batch-norm step counters and unwraps the paired release's model. prefix when given that file instead.

The SIDD width-32 denoiser. The GoPro and REDS variants (IK_VAL_NAFNET_GOPRO / _REDS) are separate .pth files at the same repo, fetched by hand; only the SIDD one the native-reader parity test uses is tracked here.
The released HDv3 IFNet. The .pkl is a modern torch zip; the converter renames the block/head Sequentials and drops the teacher subtrees.
big-lama, distributed as a zip. `extract` names the checkpoint inside it (the Lightning best.ckpt); fetch.py downloads the archive and pulls that member out as the raw file.
The photographic MODNet, served only from Google Drive. `gdrive` is the file id; fetch.py fetches it with gdown (pip install gdown). The HF ONNX exports remain unreadable by this loader.

YOLOv8 nano. The .pt pickles a live ultralytics DetectionModel tree; the native reader walks its nn.Module state (no ultralytics classes constructed) rather than needing the package the converter imports. The larger variants (yolo-l/x, IK_VAL_YOLO_LARGE/_XLARGE) are separate .pt files, fetched by hand.

unresolved.note: fast-neural-style `mosaic.pth` is no longer served: download.pytorch.org/models/fast_neural_style/{mosaic.pth,saved_models.zip}, the S3 path, and the web.archive copy all 403/404 as of 2026-08-19, and the only HF hit is an ExecuTorch .pte this loader cannot read. A SEEDED checkpoint from the reference `transformer_net.py` was tried and REJECTED: the network is trained to emit 0...255, so with random weights its output is near-zero noise (range about +-1.5 before the divide by 255) and the cosine measures the port's noise floor rather than the model — it scored 0.68, which looks like a failure and means nothing. Same trap as matting on a synthetic plate. The recorded 0.9999926 was measured on the official checkpoint; re-running it needs that file to reappear or a mirror to be found.

sources.comment: Reference implementations the oracles import. `IK_REF_SRC` points at <root>/refsrc; the three models whose reference is a whole small package get their own variable. Paths are relative to the source root. The sam2 entries reconstruct the package the SAM 2 oracles import: it cannot be pip-installed here (it needs Python >= 3.10) and was previously vendored by hand, which left that oracle unreproducible. An entry with an empty URL is an empty __init__.py.

releases_comment: A diffusion release is a directory of files rather than one checkpoint, so it is fetched whole and used in place — the port's `NFKMLXSDReleaseFiles(directoryURL:)` reads the released tree directly, and no conversion step applies. `text_encoder` and `vae` files a release publishes in half precision load through `NFKMLXWeightPrecision.float32`, which is the precision the parity records were measured at.

releases.note: The reference text-to-image pipeline for the `sd_text_encoder`, `sd_tokenizer`, and `sd_text_to_image` oracles.

stabilityai/stable-diffusion-2-1-base is GATED and returns 401 without a credential. This is an ungated release of the same lineage and geometry (cross-attention 1024, heads [5, 10, 20, 20], linear projection, OpenCLIP text tower), at the 768 v-prediction settings — which also exercises the sampler's velocity path. Its `model_index.json` names a safety checker whose `feature_extractor/` it does not ship, so those two entries are removed before the reference pipeline loads it. Its text encoder and autoencoder are published in bfloat16.
Published only in half precision; every parity run loads it at float32.

The smallest Qwen3 dense decoder, 1.4 GB. Its checkpoint ships lm_head.weight even though tie_word_embeddings is true; the two tensors are byte-identical, so the loader drops the duplicate rather than building a projection the tied model does not have.

The Qwen3-0.6B dense decoder fine-tuned as a text embedder, 1.2 GB. Its architecture is Qwen3ForCausalLM (model_type qwen3), so NFKMLXLanguage.configuration reads it unchanged; the embedder reads the base model's last hidden state, pools the LAST token (the tokenizer appends <|endoftext|>, whose position it reads), and L2-normalizes. Its embedding vocabulary is 151669, and its embeddings are tied.

EmbeddingGemma-300M, 1.2 GB. google/embeddinggemma-300m is gated; unsloth/embeddinggemma-300m is a faithful ungated mirror (the project uses mirrors for gated repos, as SD 2.1 does). The backbone is Gemma3TextModel (model_type gemma3_text) with use_bidirectional_attention true, NOT the causal Gemma 4 (gemma4_text) NFKMLXGemmaLanguage implements: `(1+w)` RMS norm (Gemma 3), sandwich norms, dual RoPE (local 10000 / global 1000000), sliding-window pattern 6 (window 512), QK-norm, GeGLU gelu_tanh, no value norm, no per-layer embeddings, no softcapping. The sentence-transformers head is mean pooling → Dense 768->3072 → Dense 3072->768 (both no-bias, Identity) → L2. Prompts: query 'task: search result | query: ', document 'title: none | text: '.

gte-reranker-modernbert-base, 0.6 GB. A ModernBertForSequenceClassification cross-encoder reranker: a bidirectional ModernBERT encoder over a [CLS] query [SEP] document [SEP] pair, mean-pooled, through a prediction head (dense + gelu + LayerNorm) and a single-logit classifier -> a relevance score. ModernBERT is RoPE (global theta 160000 every 3rd layer, local theta 10000 with a 128 sliding window elsewhere), GeGLU (Wi -> input,gate; act(input)*gate), LayerNorm throughout (norm_bias false), bias-free attention/mlp, no absolute position embeddings; layer 0's attn_norm is Identity (embeddings are pre-normed). Tokenizer is byte-level BPE (GPT-2 family), which the core NFKByteLevelBPETokenizer reads; the release ships only tokenizer.json, so vocab.json/merges.txt are extracted from it.

SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct, 2.0 GB (Apache, ungated). SmolVLMForConditionalGeneration: a SigLIP vision encoder (hidden 768, patch 16, image 512) -> pixel-shuffle connector (scale_factor 4: 768*16=12288 -> Linear -> 960) -> a Llama decoder (VLlama3ForCausalLM, hidden 960, 32 layers, 15 heads, 5 kv, head_dim 64, tie true, model_type llama, which NFKMLXLanguageNet reads). image_token_id 49190 marks where the projected vision tokens splice into the text embeddings. Oracle: transformers' own SmolVLMForConditionalGeneration + AutoProcessor.

SmolLM2-135M-Instruct Q4_K_M GGUF, 105 MB (a small real quantized LLM). The test source for the native GGUF reader: a Q4_K_M model mixes Q4_K (most weights), Q6_K (embeddings/output), Q8_0, and F32 (norms), so one file exercises every dequantizer. IK_VAL_GGUF points at the file (config value is the relative path, joined to the directory).

Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, 4.25 GB. Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration: a qwen3_vl ViT (depth 24, hidden 1024, 2D rotary, spatial_merge_size 2, deepstack layers 5/11/17) + a qwen3_vl_text decoder (Qwen3 blocks, hidden 2048/28 layers, but M-RoPE interleaved mrope_section [24,20,20] and deepstack injection at decoder layers 0/1/2). image_token_id 151655. Far more than SmolVLM: M-RoPE 3D positions and deepstack are real additions to the reused Qwen3 decoder.

The next dense Gemma 4 size: 42 layers, hidden 2560, 2 KV heads, kv-shared 18. 16 GB of bf16, which doubles past this machine's RAM at float32 - so its oracle runs under IK_GEMMA_DTYPE=bfloat16 and the Swift side loads at .checkpoint precision.

Structural only, like the Flash entry: shapes.json is built from the headers of the shards covering layers 0/3/60 plus the globals, fetched by HTTP range request (~1 MB against 400+ GB). The weights are never downloaded.

The LJSpeech-trained conformer FastSpeech2 and its 78-symbol ARPAbet vocabulary - the matching phoneme table the TTS chain needs. IK_VAL_FASTSPEECH2 is the .bin converted to safetensors (a passthrough that drops num_batches_tracked); the transformers implementation is the oracle.

MiniMax Music 3, the Diffusers-format release, fetched component by component as the port lands each stage (vocoder so far; condition_encoder, rvq_depth_decoder, transformer, language_model follow). The official checkpoint is already safetensors, so it is used in place: the Swift loader fuses the weight-norm pairs and transposes the conv layouts itself, and the diffusers implementation (>= 0.40.0, MiniMaxMusic3Vocoder et al.) is the oracle. THE WEIGHTS ARE NOT PERMISSIVELY LICENSED - the MiniMax-Music3 Community License requires UI attribution in commercial products and separate authorization above USD 20M yearly revenue; see Docs/companions.md and the LICENSE fetched beside the weights.
The multilingual byte-level BPE vocabulary, which the voice loop-closure test uses to read Whisper's transcription of the synthesized speech.

The LTX-Video DiT (2B), the denoising transformer. ~7.7 GB sharded. Loads directly (module keys mirror LTXVideoTransformer3DModel). Parity via run_reference.py ltx_transformer under the ltx oracle env, feeding recorded text embeddings (no T5).

T5-XXL v1.1 text encoder for LTX-Video (also the text encoder family for Wan/PixArt/SD3/Flux). ~19 GB fp32 sharded. Loads directly (keys mirror T5EncoderModel). Parity via run_reference.py ltx_t5 under the ltx oracle env.

oracle_environments.comment: diffusers cannot be installed beside the other oracles — it needs a newer transformers than the 4.33.3 the Whisper / CLIP / SegFormer records were measured against — so the `sd_*` modes of Tools/reference-parity/run_reference.py run under their own interpreter.

diffusers.create: python3 -m venv sdvenv && ./sdvenv/bin/pip install "diffusers==0.31.0" "transformers==4.46.3" "torch==2.8.0" safetensors accelerate

llm.why: Qwen3 needs transformers >= 4.51; the vision oracles run against 4.33.3 and the diffusers oracle against its own environment, so a third one keeps them from fighting. The SmolVLM oracle additionally needs Pillow, torchvision, and num2words for its image processor.
llm.rebuild: python3 -m venv ~/.inferkit-validation/llmvenv && ~/.inferkit-validation/llmvenv/bin/python3 -m pip install 'transformers>=4.51' torch safetensors Pillow torchvision num2words gguf accelerate 'silero-vad' 'torchaudio==2.8.0' 'descript-audio-codec' 'snac'

music.why: MiniMax Music 3's official implementation is in diffusers >= 0.40.0 (MiniMaxMusic3Vocoder, MiniMaxMusic3RVQDepthDecoder, MiniMaxMusic3ConditionEncoder, the flow-matching DiT), which cannot share the pinned diffusers 0.31.0 the SD records were measured against, so the music_* modes run under their own interpreter.
music.rebuild: /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.12/bin/python3.12 -m venv ~/.inferkit-validation/musicvenv && ~/.inferkit-validation/musicvenv/bin/python3 -m pip install 'diffusers==0.40.0' 'transformers>=5' torch safetensors accelerate

gemma.why: Gemma 4 is in no released transformers, and the version that has it requires Python 3.10; this machine's system Python is 3.9.6, so Homebrew's python@3.12 was installed alongside it and this environment built on that. It also carries the deepseek_quant oracle: torch 2.13 is the first here with float8_e4m3fn and float8_e8m0fnu on the CPU, and ml_dtypes supplies float4_e2m1fn, which torch has no CPU kernel for.
gemma.rebuild: brew install python@3.12 && /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.12/bin/python3.12 -m venv ~/.inferkit-validation/gemmavenv && ~/.inferkit-validation/gemmavenv/bin/python3 -m pip install 'git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git@main' torch safetensors ml_dtypes

ltx.create: python3 -m venv ~/.inferkit-validation/ltxvenv && ~/.inferkit-validation/ltxvenv/bin/pip install 'diffusers>=0.32' 'transformers>=4.44' torch safetensors accelerate
ltx.why: AutoencoderKLLTXVideo needs diffusers >= 0.32, newer than the sd/other oracles.
